key_insight: The paper introduces MSVR, a variance-reduction estimator that can track many coupled inner functions while probing only a few blocks per iteration, enabling faster optimization for finite-sum coupled compositional problems.
engineering_relevance: This matters for large-scale learning systems where nested objectives and limited oracle access make standard full tracking too expensive, including multi-task and compositional deep optimization workloads.
method: Proposes a Multi-block-Single-probe Variance Reduction (MSVR) estimator to update only sampled blocks of g(w) efficiently.
Builds FCCO optimization algorithms on top of MSVR for non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL settings.
Shows improved dependence on m when outer gradients ∇f_i are linear.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved sample complexities across multiple objective classes and empirical gains on multi-task deep AUC maximization.
watch_item: Performance depends on partial block sampling and stochastic oracle assumptions, so implementation quality and the number of probed blocks may strongly affect practical gains.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
